reasons: Only visible candidate; portfolio cannot establish variation.
Mass reads as one stepped carved monolith, too close to a single chassis family.
Ground threshold is present but not sufficiently program-specific for neighborhood active edge.
Upper stepping repeats the same family logic instead of creating a distinct section/void relation.

rationale: This board does not function as a portfolio because it presents only one candidate and one dominant family. The visible mass is a carved, stepped monolith with a frontage notch; that is legible, but it does not establish a comparative set, nor does it demonstrate the required variety of spatial identities for a neighborhood mixed-use contact sheet. For the next run, anchor the board with different macro relations—one courtyard/cut, one split-wing or lift, one terrace/setback—so the ground threshold remains active while upper massing becomes genuinely differentiated.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: single carved-stepped monolith with cut-corner/notched frontage and recursive stepped roof; one dominant box/bar chassis

required_next_relations: Keep the active street edge, but rework the mass so the public void is structurally legible and program-driven rather than a generic notch.
Introduce a clearly different spatial family from the current stepped monolith: a split-wing court, carved void, lift with public base, or a bent bar with a true threshold.
Preserve calm upper massing while changing the sectional move so the next candidate is not another box/bar variation.
Ensure the next board shows at least 3 materially distinct candidate families with one clear public void/terrace relation.
Use access-bound geometry that makes the west street edge readable without relying on repeated stepped roof treatment.
